claims.text: This paper addresses the critical challenge of uncertainty estimation in NeRFs for safety-critical applications.

The authors introduce a probabilistic approach that quantifies both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties from a single forward pass without compromising rendering quality or incurring significant computational overhead.
The method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on three standardized benchmarks for both scene reconstruction fidelity and uncertainty estimation quality.
Seamless integration of uncertainty quantification with NeRF rendering
Direct quantification of both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties
State-of-the-art performance on standardized benchmarks
TimeNeRF presents a generalizable neural rendering approach for novel view synthesis at arbitrary viewpoints and times from few input views.
The method combines multi-view stereo, neural radiance fields, and disentanglement strategies to enable smooth temporal transitions, particularly capturing natural scene changes from dawn to dusk.
This work addresses the gap in temporal 3D scene modeling and introduces capabilities for metaverse applications requiring immersive day-night transitions.
Few-shot generalization without per-scene optimization
Smooth temporal transitions in natural scenes
Integration of multi-view stereo with NeRF
This comparative study examines three accelerated NeRF variants (DS-NeRF, TensoRF, and HashNeRF) for low-compute, low-data regimes.
The authors explore depth-supervised TensoRF, ablate feature-decoding MLP architectures, and propose four HashNeRF variants with residual and convolutional designs.
While no extensions conclusively outperform baselines under iso-time evaluation, the work characterizes design tradeoffs for constrained settings.
Comparative analysis of accelerated NeRF variants
Depth-supervision loss integration with TensoRF
Architectural ablation studies for HashNeRF
Characterization of low-compute regime tradeoffs
This pioneering work addresses lens flare removal using a multi-view NeRF framework.
GN-FR leverages the view-dependent nature of flare artifacts to recover details obscured in individual images.

The framework incorporates Flare-occupancy Mask Generation, View Sampler, and Point Sampler modules within the Generalizable NeRF Transformer, utilizing a novel masking loss function for unsupervised learning.
The authors also introduce a 3D multi-view flare dataset with 17 real scenes and 782 images.
First NeRF-based flare removal framework
Multi-view approach to ill-posed flare removal problem
Unsupervised learning with masking loss function
Novel 3D multi-view flare dataset
This comprehensive survey compiles key theoretical advancements in NeRFs, alternative scene representations, and emerging challenges.
It explores applications in reconstruction, examines NeRFs' impact on computer vision and robotics, and reviews essential datasets and toolkits.
The survey identifies literature gaps and provides directions for future research, serving as a valuable resource for understanding NeRF's evolution and real-world deployment.
Comprehensive compilation of NeRF advancements
Analysis of alternative scene representations
Review of applications in computer vision and robotics
Identification of open challenges and future directions
This work proposes a satellite-specific NeRF model capable of obtaining three-dimensional semantic representations from multi-date satellite images with pixel-wise semantic labels.

The approach demonstrates robustness in improving noisy input labels and enhances color prediction by utilizing semantic information to address temporal inconsistencies from non-stationary categories.
The authors present a dataset with manually generated labels for popular multi-view satellite images.
Neural semantic field generation from satellite imagery
Robustness to noisy input labels
Temporal inconsistency handling for non-stationary objects
Novel satellite dataset with manual semantic labels
NeuGen integrates a brain-inspired normalization technique into leading NeRF architectures (MVSNeRF and GeoNeRF) to enhance domain generalization.
By extracting domain-invariant features, NeuGen improves accuracy and robustness in image rendering across diverse scenes.

Comprehensive evaluations confirm superior generalizability and rendering quality compared to existing models, demonstrating the potential of merging neuroscientific principles with deep learning frameworks.
Seamless integration with existing NeRF architectures
Improved generalization across diverse datasets
This paper addresses NeRF's limitation in handling complex planar reflections, which are often misinterpreted as erroneous geometries.
The reflection-aware NeRF jointly models planar reflectors and explicitly casts reflected rays to capture high-frequency reflections.
Sparse edge regularization prevents duplicate scene representations, enabling accurate geometry reconstruction and clean reflection-free views while reconstructing highly detailed reflections.
Joint modeling of planar reflectors and reflected rays
Single radiance field for primary and reflected color rendering
Sparse edge regularization for accurate geometry
Enhanced performance on real-world reflection datasets
MaintaAvatar addresses the practical challenge of updating human avatars while maintaining rendering quality for past appearances.
The model utilizes a Global-Local Joint Storage Module and Pose Distillation Module to resolve catastrophic forgetting and color bleeding issues.
The approach requires only limited data collection for quick fine-tuning, achieving maintainable virtual avatars suitable for real-world scenarios where appearances and poses constantly change.
Continual learning framework for NeRF-based avatars
Pose Distillation Module for pose accuracy
Prevention of catastrophic forgetting and color bleeding
ShinyNeRF introduces a novel framework for handling both isotropic and anisotropic reflections, addressing the challenge of modeling anisotropic specular surfaces such as brushed metals.
The method jointly estimates surface normals, tangents, specular concentration, and anisotropy magnitudes using Anisotropic Spherical Gaussian distributions.
Experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in digitizing anisotropic specular reflections with plausible physical interpretations and material property editing capabilities.
Joint isotropic and anisotropic reflection modeling
Anisotropic Spherical Gaussian distribution learning
Physical parameter estimation (normals, tangents, concentration)
Robustness and Reliability: Evidential NeRF addresses uncertainty quantification, critical for safety-critical applications [citation: Duan & Wong, 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23574v2).
Temporal Dynamics: TimeNeRF extends NeRF capabilities to temporal domains, enabling smooth transitions across time [citation: Hung et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13929v1).
Accessibility: Low-Cost NeRF research focuses on making NeRF technology more accessible through reduced computational requirements [citation: Huang et al., 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09312v1).

Domain Specificity: Specialized applications emerge in satellite imagery [citation: Wagner et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16992v1), avatar creation [citation: Gu et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.02372v1), and cultural heritage digitization [citation: Barreiro et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.21692v2).

Generalization: Multiple works address domain generalization challenges through novel architectures and learning strategies [citation: Qazi et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06894v1; Hung et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13929v1).
